analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the public-health problem of transfusion-transmitted infections in multi-transfused patients in southern Iran, where the knowledge gap was the seroprevalence of human T-cell lymphotropic virus (HTLV) in these high-risk groups. The stated objective was to determine HTLV seroprevalence among patients with β-thalassemia major and those on regular hemodialysis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted in five cities in southern Iran (Dashtestan, Bushehr, Genaveh, Tangestan, and Kangan) between 2023 and 2024. It enrolled all patients with β-thalassemia major and those on regular hemodialysis receiving transfusions, alongside healthy controls.
analysis.methods: Serum samples were screened for HTLV-I/II antibodies using ELISA, with positive results confirmed by Western Blot. Hepatitis-related markers (anti-HCV, anti-HEV IgG, HBsAb, HBV infection criteria) were assessed using serological assays.
analysis.main_results: Among 134 thalassemia patients, 6 (4.48%, 95% CI: 1.83%-9.91%) were HTLV-I/II seropositive, all confirmed as HTLV-1 by Western blot. Hemodialysis patients and controls were HTLV-negative. Among HTLV-1 seropositive thalassemia patients, 4 (66.7%) were anti-HCV positive, 2 (33.4%) were anti-HEV IgG positive, and 5 (83.33%) had HBsAb.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the 4.48% HTLV-1 seroprevalence in thalassemia patients as relatively high and indicative of elevated exposure risk in this population. The novelty lies in documenting HTLV-1 seropositivity in a thalassemia cohort in southern Iran, contrasting with the absence of HTLV in hemodialysis patients and controls.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support targeted HTLV donor screening to reduce transfusion-transmitted HTLV-1 infection in thalassemia patients, given their reliance on frequent transfusions. The study also highlights co-infections (HCV, HEV) in HTLV-1 seropositive patients, underscoring the need for integrated screening.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, small sample size, and lack of adjustment for confounding factors in the association analyses. The evidence is moderate due to these constraints and the absence of longitudinal follow-up.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study in southern Iran assessed HTLV seroprevalence among multi-transfused patients with β-thalassemia major and those on hemodialysis. Among 134 thalassemia patients, 4.48% (95% CI: 1.83%-9.91%) were HTLV-1 seropositive by ELISA and Western blot, while hemodialysis patients and controls were negative. Co-infections with HCV (66.7%) and HEV (33.4%) were observed in HTLV-1 seropositive thalassemia patients, and 83.33% had HBsAb. The authors highlight a relatively high HTLV-1 exposure risk in thalassemia patients and recommend HTLV donor screening to mitigate transfusion-transmitted infection. Limitations include the small sample size, cross-sectional design, and lack of confounding adjustment, warranting cautious interpretation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Healthcare workers (HCWs) are at increased risk of exposure to vaccine-preventable diseases, including hepatitis B, tuberculosis (TB), and tetanus, due to their occupational environment. This study aimed to determine the vaccination coverage for hepatitis B, tuberculosis, and tetanus among HCWs in district hospitals in Yaounde, Cameroon, and to identify factors associated with incomplete vaccination.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted from January to June 2024 across all seven district hospitals in Yaounde, enrolling a total of 406 HCWs using a structured, self-administered questionnaire.
analysis.methods: Data were collected using a structured, self-administered questionnaire and analyzed using R Statistics version 4.3.3. Bivariate and multivariate logistic regression models were used to identify predictors of incomplete vaccination, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05.
analysis.main_results: Full vaccination coverage was 36.2% for hepatitis B, 15.8% for tuberculosis, and 53.4% for tetanus. Multivariate analysis revealed that HCWs aged 55-66 years were significantly less likely to be incompletely vaccinated against hepatitis B compared to those aged 19-29 years (aOR = 0.07; 95% CI: 0.01-0.39; p = 0.004). Nurses and laboratory technicians were more likely to be incompletely vaccinated than doctors (aOR = 7.06; 95% CI: 3.82-13.6; p < 0.001 and aOR = 3.78; 95% CI: 1.73-8.52; p = 0.001, respectively).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Vaccination coverage for hepatitis B, tuberculosis, and tetanus among HCWs in Yaounde remains suboptimal, particularly for hepatitis B. The study identified specific factors associated with incomplete vaccination, including age, profession, and length of professional experience.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the need for targeted interventions to improve vaccination coverage among HCWs, particularly addressing financial barriers, improving access to vaccines, and implementing educational interventions to enhance vaccine uptake and protect both HCWs and their patients from preventable occupational infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study did not report on the generalisability of the findings to other regions or healthcare settings. The evidence strength is moderate due to the cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported data.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to determine the vaccination coverage for hepatitis B, tuberculosis, and tetanus among healthcare workers (HCWs) in district hospitals in Yaounde, Cameroon, and to identify factors associated with incomplete vaccination. A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted from January to June 2024 across all seven district hospitals in Yaounde, enrolling a total of 406 HCWs using a structured, self-administered questionnaire. Data were analyzed using R Statistics version 4.3.3, with bivariate and multivariate logistic regression models used to identify predictors of incomplete vaccination. The results showed that full vaccination coverage was 36.2% for hepatitis B, 15.8% for tuberculosis, and 53.4% for tetanus. Multivariate analysis revealed that HCWs aged 55-66 years were significantly less likely to be incompletely vaccinated against hepatitis B compared to those aged 19-29 years (aOR = 0.07; 95% CI: 0.01-0.39; p = 0.004). Nurses and laboratory technicians were more likely to be incompletely vaccinated than doctors (aOR = 7.06; 95% CI: 3.82-13.6; p < 0.001 and aOR = 3.78; 95% CI: 1.73-8.52; p = 0.001, respectively). The study concluded that vaccination coverage for these diseases among HCWs in Yaounde remains suboptimal, particularly for hepatitis B. The findings highlight the need for targeted interventions to improve vaccination coverage, addressing financial barriers, improving access to vaccines, and implementing educational interventions to enhance vaccine uptake and protect both HCWs and their patients from preventable occupational infections. The study did not report on the generalisability of the findings to other regions or healthcare settings, and the evidence strength is moderate due to the cross-sectional design and reliance on self-reported data.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is associated with immune tolerance mediated by HBV e antigen (HBeAg), yet the spatial 3D genomic and epigenetic mechanisms underlying macrophage dysfunction remain poorly understood. The study aimed to elucidate how HBeAg reprograms macrophage chromatin architecture and transcriptional programs to drive immune evasion.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study integrated RNA-sequencing, high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C), and chromatin immunoprecipitation-sequencing (ChIP-seq) to analyze control and HBeAg-stimulated macrophages. Key findings were cross-validated using human HBV-infected datasets.
analysis.methods: RNA-seq, Hi-C, and ChIP-seq were used to map the topological and transcriptional regulatory landscape in macrophages exposed to HBeAg. Epigenetic reprogramming was analyzed through H3K27ac enhancer deposition, CTCF-mediated structural boundary alterations, and HLTF-associated H3K27me3 gene silencing.
analysis.main_results: HBeAg stimulation robustly activated pro-inflammatory transcriptional programs, with the TNF signaling pathway identified as a central node. Hi-C revealed global 3D chromatin reorganization, including inactive-to-active compartment switching, de novo H3K27ac enhancer accumulation, and topologically associating domain (TAD) restructuring such as TAD merging.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that HBeAg orchestrates a hierarchical restructuring of the 3D genome and targeted epigenetic reprogramming to induce macrophage dysfunction. Novel mechanistic insights include the identification of structural variants and core spatial-target genes (e.g., MET, FLNB, BLVRB) as potential therapeutic targets.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeting the identified epigenetic and chromatin structural alterations may offer therapeutic strategies for HBV-related liver diseases by modulating macrophage-mediated immune tolerance.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro macrophage models and cross-validation with human datasets, which may not fully capture in vivo complexity. The evidence strength is moderate due to the abstract-only scope and lack of functional validation of identified targets.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated how HBV e antigen (HBeAg) reprograms macrophage chromatin architecture and transcriptional programs to drive immune evasion in chronic hepatitis B infection. Using RNA-seq, Hi-C, and ChIP-seq, the authors demonstrated that HBeAg robustly activates pro-inflammatory pathways, particularly TNF signaling, while inducing global 3D chromatin reorganization. Key mechanisms included inactive-to-active compartment switching, de novo enhancer accumulation, and topologically associating domain restructuring. Epigenetic reprogramming involved H3K27ac deposition, CTCF-mediated boundary alterations, and HLTF-associated gene silencing. The identified structural variants and spatial-target genes (e.g., MET, FLNB, BLVRB) were proposed as novel therapeutic targets for HBV-related liver diseases. However, the study’s abstract-only scope and reliance on in vitro models limit the generalizability of findings, warranting further in vivo validation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: HBV-related acute-on-chronic liver failure (HBV-ACLF) carries high short-term mortality, and existing prognostic models have limitations, leaving an unmet need for an improved predictive tool.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study enrolled 1,170 HBV-ACLF patients admitted to a single Chinese center between 2008 and 2023, randomly split into a development cohort (n=822) and a validation cohort (n=348).
analysis.methods: Predictive factors for 28-day and 90-day mortality were identified using Cox regression, and two new prognostic scores (AHF-MELD and AHN-MELD) were developed and compared against established models using ROC, calibration, and decision curve analyses.
analysis.main_results: The AHF-MELD and AHN-MELD scores showed stronger predictive capacity than MELD, MELD-sodium, CLIF-C OF and AARC scores and were comparable to CLIF-C ACLF, COSSH ACLF and COSSH ACLF II scores, with good calibration and net benefit across thresholds.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that AHF-MELD and AHN-MELD scores may serve as potential predictive tools for short-term prognosis in HBV-ACLF, representing an advance over conventional models by demonstrating superior or comparable performance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These scores could inform risk stratification and clinical decision-making for HBV-ACLF patients, potentially improving short-term prognostic accuracy in resource-limited settings where advanced models are unavailable.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The single-center, retrospective design and lack of external validation limit generalizability, and reliance on abstract-only evidence constrains detailed assessment of statistical robustness and potential biases.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed and validated two novel prognostic scores (AHF-MELD and AHN-MELD) for HBV-related acute-on-chronic liver failure (HBV-ACLF) using a retrospective cohort of 1,170 patients from a single Chinese center. Cox regression identified predictors of 28-day and 90-day mortality, and the new scores outperformed conventional models (MELD, MELD-sodium, CLIF-C OF, AARC) while matching more advanced scores (CLIF-C ACLF, COSSH ACLF, COSSH ACLF II) in predictive capacity. Calibration and decision curve analyses indicated good model fit and clinical net benefit across thresholds. The authors conclude these scores may serve as potential tools for short-term prognosis in HBV-ACLF, offering a practical alternative where complex models are impractical. However, the single-center design, retrospective nature, and absence of external validation limit generalizability, and reliance on abstract-only evidence constrains a full assessment of methodological rigor.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the prognostic significance of genetic variants in nucleotide metabolism genes for patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), a gap in understanding how these variants influence survival outcomes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cohort study was conducted involving 866 HBV-HCC patients to evaluate associations between genetic variants in 94 nucleotide metabolism-related genes and overall survival.
analysis.methods: Cox proportional hazards regression analyses were performed to assess associations, with multiple testing correction using Bayesian false discovery probability and false-positive report probability. Luciferase reporter assays were used to evaluate allele-specific regulatory effects on gene expression.
analysis.main_results: Two single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), DCTD rs17074255 G>A (HR = 1.22, 95% CI: 1.06–1.40, p = 0.005) and ENTPD2 rs3763662 G>A (HR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.03–1.34, p = 0.015), were significantly associated with poorer overall survival. A dose-dependent association between the number of risk genotypes and poorer survival was observed (Ptrend < 0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that ENTPD2 rs3763662 and DCTD rs17074255 may serve as prognostic indicators for HBV-HCC through regulation of mRNA expression, supported by functional and expression data. This provides new insights into the role of nucleotide metabolism-related genetic variation in HBV-HCC progression.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest potential for prognostic assessment in HBV-HCC patients, pending replication in independent cohorts, which could inform future surveillance or risk stratification strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on a single cohort and lack of external validation, which constrains generalizability and strength of evidence. The abstract-only evidence base further limits detailed methodological and result assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether genetic variants in nucleotide metabolism genes predict survival in 866 HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients using Cox regression and multiple testing corrections. Two SNPs, DCTD rs17074255 and ENTPD2 rs3763662, were significantly associated with poorer overall survival, with a dose-dependent effect observed for the number of risk genotypes. Functional assays showed allele-specific regulatory effects of rs3763662 on ENTPD2 expression, and elevated expression of both genes correlated with worse survival in external datasets. The authors propose these variants as potential prognostic indicators, though replication in independent cohorts is needed to confirm utility.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review evaluates postoperative adjuvant therapies for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) following curative-intent hepatic resection, focusing on efficacy and safety outcomes. The central question addresses the comparative ranking of adjuvant therapies in terms of recurrence-free survival (RFS), overall survival (OS), and adverse events.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic review with network meta-analysis (NMA) was conducted, including randomized controlled trials identified via searches of MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase, CENTRAL, Web of Science, Scopus, regional databases, clinical trial registries, and conference proceedings. The review included 28 randomized controlled trials involving 4,830 participants and employed a frequentist NMA to estimate pooled hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Treatments were ranked using P-scores.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Internal radiation and brachytherapy approaches (125 I-brachytherapy, IMRT, and 131 I-metuximab) were associated with the greatest reductions in mortality compared with observation. For RFS, autologous formalin-fixed tumor vaccine (AFTV) ranked highest, followed by adjuvant Cidan capsule plus TACE, 125 I-brachytherapy, and IMRT. Most therapies demonstrated manageable toxicity, with immune checkpoint inhibitors showing a favorable benefit-risk profile.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The evidence for the strongest OS benefit (125 I-brachytherapy, IMRT, and 131 I-metuximab) is based on limited data from single small trials, which the authors consider hypothesis-generating rather than definitive. The review does not report subgroup analyses by etiology (e.g., hepatitis B vs. C) or liver function status beyond Child–Pugh A classification.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings support risk-adapted integration of radiotherapy and immunotherapy after resection, but further large-scale head-to-head trials are needed to validate these results. Priority should be given to trials comparing AFTV, adjuvant Cidan capsule plus TACE, and internal radiation therapies directly against standard observation or placebo.

analysis.summary_en: This network meta-analysis compares postoperative adjuvant therapies for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) after curative resection, focusing on recurrence-free survival (RFS), overall survival (OS), and safety. Based on 28 randomized controlled trials (n=4,830), internal radiation and brachytherapy (125 I-brachytherapy, IMRT, 131 I-metuximab) showed the greatest OS benefit, while autologous formalin-fixed tumor vaccine (AFTV) and adjuvant Cidan capsule plus TACE ranked highest for RFS. Most therapies had manageable toxicity, with immune checkpoint inhibitors demonstrating a favorable benefit-risk profile. However, the strongest OS benefits were derived from single small trials, limiting definitive conclusions. The review supports risk-adapted integration of radiotherapy and immunotherapy but emphasizes the need for large-scale head-to-head trials to validate these findings.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Congenital infections in the TORCH complex contribute to fetal and neonatal morbidity and mortality, yet data on prenatal TORCH screening uptake and its socio-demographic determinants in Romania are limited. This study addressed the public health need to quantify self-reported TORCH testing and identify factors influencing its use among pregnant women in Romania.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional observational study recruited 1301 pregnant women in Romania via online self-administered questionnaires distributed through social media and pregnancy-related forums between August 2022 and March 2023. Participants were pregnant women residing in Romania who completed the survey.
analysis.methods: Associations between socio-demographic, obstetrical, and prenatal care factors and self-reported TORCH testing were assessed using chi-square tests and multivariable binary logistic regression models, reporting odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
analysis.main_results: Overall, 75.6% reported undergoing serological testing for at least one TORCH-related infection, and 49.3% reported a complete TORCH panel. Testing was most frequent for Toxoplasma gondii (92.8%) and rubella virus (89.9%), and least for HSV (42.5%). Lower educational level (aOR = 0.08; 95% CI: 0.03–0.19), unemployment (aOR = 0.70; 95% CI: 0.50–0.99), and multiparity (aOR = 0.62; 95% CI: 0.49–0.77) were associated with reduced testing, while participation in prenatal education programs increased uptake (aOR = 1.37; 95% CI: 1.04–1.80).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as indicating that socio-educational and behavioral factors, rather than the frequency of prenatal consultations, predominantly influence TORCH screening uptake in Romania. The study highlights significant inequalities in access to preventive prenatal investigations, particularly among women with lower educational and socio-economic status.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that strengthening prenatal education programs and improving equitable access to standardized prenatal screening could optimize congenital infection prevention and maternal–fetal health outcomes in Romania.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The online recruitment strategy and predominantly urban, highly educated sample likely overestimate population-level screening coverage, limiting generalizability. The evidence is moderate due to potential selection bias and reliance on self-reported data without clinical verification.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study evaluated self-reported prenatal TORCH screening uptake among 1301 pregnant women in Romania using an online questionnaire distributed from August 2022 to March 2023. Overall, 75.6% reported undergoing testing for at least one TORCH-related infection, with 49.3% completing a full panel. Testing was most common for Toxoplasma gondii (92.8%) and rubella virus (89.9%), and least for HSV (42.5%). Multivariable analysis identified lower educational level (aOR 0.08), unemployment (aOR 0.70), and multiparity (aOR 0.62) as factors associated with reduced testing, while participation in prenatal education programs increased uptake (aOR 1.37). The authors conclude that socio-educational and behavioral factors, rather than the number of prenatal consultations, predominantly influence screening behavior. They recommend strengthening prenatal education and improving equitable access to standardized screening to enhance congenital infection prevention. However, the online recruitment and urban, highly educated sample likely overestimate coverage, and reliance on self-reported data limits generalizability.

analysis.time: The research was published on July 13, 2026, in the international journal *Journal of Medical Virology*. The study utilized CRISPR/Cas13a and Cas12a detection technologies combined with reverse transcription isothermal amplification (RT-RAA) to establish a portable and visualized detection method for HDV RNA and HBV DNA.
analysis.location_and_population: The research team is based at Beijing You'an Hospital (Capital Medical University Affiliated Beijing You'an Hospital/Beijing Institute of Liver Diseases) and includes researchers from the Academy of Military Medical Sciences and Xinjiang Yili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture Xinhua Hospital. The validation involved 70 patient samples.
analysis.event: A research team led by Professor Ren Feng from Beijing You'an Hospital published a paper in the *Journal of Medical Virology* establishing a novel dual portable and visualized detection method for Hepatitis D Virus (HDV) RNA and Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) DNA using CRISPR-Cas13a/Cas12a and RT-RAA technologies.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The study achieved a positive detection rate of 85.7% (60/70) for both HDV RNA and HBV DNA using the dual fluorescence method and 82.9% (58/70) using the dual lateral flow strip method. The method is characterized by high sensitivity, high specificity, low time consumption, and ease of operation. It provides a new tool for the early detection and treatment of HBV and HDV co-infection.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study has been published in an international journal. The authors optimized the detection system components and evaluated sensitivity and specificity using positive plasmids and 70 clinical samples. The method is reported to be ready for application in supporting early discovery and treatment of HBV and HDV co-infection.

analysis.brief_en: A research team led by Professor Ren Feng from Beijing You'an Hospital published a paper in the *Journal of Medical Virology* on July 13, 2026, establishing a novel dual portable and visualized detection method for Hepatitis D Virus (HDV) RNA and Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) DNA. Utilizing CRISPR-Cas13a/Cas12a and RT-RAA technologies, the method combines isothermal amplification with CRISPR detection and lateral flow strips. Validation on 70 patient samples showed a positive detection rate of 82.9% (58/70) for both viruses. The study highlights the method's high sensitivity, specificity, and operational convenience, offering a new tool for the early detection and treatment of HBV and HDV co-infection.
analysis.summary_en: A research team led by Professor Ren Feng from Beijing You'an Hospital published a paper in the *Journal of Medical Virology* on July 13, 2026, establishing a novel dual portable and visualized detection method for Hepatitis D Virus (HDV) RNA and Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) DNA. Utilizing CRISPR-Cas13a/Cas12a and RT-RAA technologies, the method combines isothermal amplification with CRISPR detection and lateral flow strips. Validation on 70 patient samples showed a positive detection rate of 82.9% (58/70) for both viruses. The study highlights the method's high sensitivity, specificity, and operational convenience, offering a new tool for the early detection and treatment of HBV and HDV co-infection.

analysis.location_and_population: Global study sites worldwide. Approximately 250 untreated HBeAg+ and HBeAg- adult subjects with chronic HBV infection (Part 1a: 131 HBeAg+ participants; Part 2a: 114 HBeAg- participants).
analysis.event: Aligos Therapeutics, a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, announced the completion of enrollment in the Phase 2 B-SUPREME study of pevifoscorvir sodium, a candidate under development for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Total enrollment of 245 participants (131 HBeAg+ and 114 HBeAg-). The study is a randomized, double-blind, active-controlled multicenter trial evaluating safety and efficacy. No current cases or deaths are reported as the study is in the enrollment phase. The risk is the ongoing development of a potential best/first-in-class oral small molecule capsid assembly modulator (CAM-E) for chronic HBV infection.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Enrollment is complete. Topline safety and efficacy data are expected in late Q3 2027. The second interim analysis for sample size re-estimation will not be performed due to over-enrollment. The study is ongoing with no unresolved information regarding the event itself, though forward-looking statements indicate risks inherent in drug development.

analysis.brief_en: Aligos Therapeutics announced on July 13, 2026, the completion of enrollment in its global Phase 2 B-SUPREME study of pevifoscorvir sodium, a candidate for chronic hepatitis B virus infection. The study enrolled 245 participants, including 131 HBeAg+ and 114 HBeAg- adults. Topline safety and efficacy data are expected in late Q3 2027. This randomized, double-blind, active-controlled trial compares pevifoscorvir sodium to tenofovir disoproxil fumarate over 48 weeks.

analysis.event: A health campaign to control and eliminate hepatitis B was held in Beijing on a Saturday. Public health officials and clinicians gathered to assess progress and map out next steps. The event is a public awareness and policy implementation initiative, not an outbreak report.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Hepatitis B remains a major public health challenge in China. The prevalence among children under five has dropped to 0.30%, while among the broader population aged 1 to 69, it stands at 5.86%. A significant proportion of those infected are unaware of their status. Chronic infection can progress to cirrhosis and liver cancer.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Since 2005, universal free infant vaccination has achieved high coverage rates (99.6% for the three-dose series and 95.6% for the timely birth dose). In September 2025, the National Disease Control and Prevention Administration and eight other departments issued an action plan for 2025–2030. Efforts are focused on maintaining high childhood vaccination rates while expanding adult immunization coverage. Grassroots health centers are playing a critical role in delivering health education, screening, and follow-up care.

analysis.time: Publication date: 2026-07-17. Event date: Not explicitly stated in the supplied evidence.
analysis.location_and_population: Chongqing Medical University (researchers), HBV transgenic mice, liver samples from patients with chronic HBV infection, HBV-replicating hepatocyte cell lines, pAAV/HBV1.2 mouse model.
analysis.event: A study published in Genes & Diseases investigated the molecular mechanisms underlying HBV-induced liver inflammation. The research identified a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-dependent signaling cascade activating the Jak2/Stat3 pathway.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The study establishes mitochondrial dysfunction-induced ROS accumulation as a pivotal trigger of HBV-associated hepatic inflammation. It identifies ROS-dependent Jak2/Stat3 activation as a promising therapeutic target for preventing inflammation-driven liver disease progression.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study was conducted using in vitro and in vivo models. Pharmacological manipulation of ROS levels (using Mito-TEMPO, NAC) confirmed the mechanism. The source is a news report summarizing a published study.

analysis.brief_en: Researchers from Chongqing Medical University have identified a specific molecular mechanism driving liver inflammation caused by chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. The study, published in Genes & Diseases, reveals that mitochondrial dysfunction leads to the accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), which activates the Jak2/Stat3 signaling pathway. This cascade triggers the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines like IL-6 and IL-8, ultimately fueling hepatic inflammation. The findings suggest that targeting this ROS-dependent pathway could offer a new therapeutic strategy to prevent the progression of HBV-induced liver disease.

analysis.time: Publication date: 2026-07-15. Event date: 2025 (coverage data). WHO-UNICEF WUENIC report released on 2026-07-15.
analysis.location_and_population: Target population: newborns within 24 hours of birth.
analysis.event: WHO and UNICEF questioned India’s official hepatitis B birth-dose coverage estimate (92% reported vs. 70% estimated by agencies) as part of the 2026 WUENIC report. The agencies flagged inconsistencies in coverage denominators and target population calculations. This is a preliminary assessment pending review of India’s NFHS-6 survey results.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: India reported 92% hepatitis B birth-dose coverage in 2025, but WHO-UNICEF estimate suggests only 70% coverage, implying ~30% of newborns missed the vaccine within 24 hours. Chronic hepatitis B risk from mother-to-child transmission remains high for unvaccinated infants. Globally, 13.5 million children were 'zero-dose' in 2025, with 750,000 fewer than in 2024.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: WHO and UNICEF are reviewing India’s NFHS-6 survey results for reconciliation. India’s routine immunisation remains high for other vaccines (e.g., DTP1 at 97%, measles at 98%). The agencies have marked the hepatitis B birth-dose estimate as 'challenged' due to denominator concerns. No official response from India’s health ministry was provided in the report.

analysis.brief_en: On 15 July 2026, WHO and UNICEF released the WUENIC report questioning India’s reported 92% coverage of the hepatitis B birth-dose vaccine in 2025, estimating actual coverage at only 70%. The agencies cited inconsistencies in target population denominators and flagged the discrepancy as ‘challenged.’ While India’s overall childhood immunisation remains strong (e.g., DTP1 at 97%, measles at 98%), the hepatitis B birth-dose gap leaves nearly 30% of newborns unprotected within 24 hours, increasing chronic infection risks. WHO and UNICEF will review India’s NFHS-6 survey results for reconciliation.

analysis.time: The Prevention of Future Deaths report was published online on 10 July 2026 (N3). The patient died on 12 September 2025 (N9). The article was published on 16 July 2026 (N2).
analysis.location_and_population: The event occurred in the UK, specifically involving a patient treated in Inner London North (N3, N9). The coroner noted a 'large population' of patients diagnosed with hepatitis B through opt-out screening in emergency departments (N2, N9).
analysis.event: An assistant coroner for Inner London North, Richard Brittain, issued a 'Prevention of Future Deaths' report following the death of a patient, Mr. Tung Tran, aged 41, due to complications from hepatitis B reactivation caused by the inadvertent discontinuation of entecavir (N3, N9).
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The patient died (N9). The coroner identified a lack of national guidance on prescribing and monitoring for hepatitis B reactivation (N3, N9). He noted a 'large population' of patients with hepatitis B from opt-out screening but a lack of specialised commissioning to maintain engagement with services (N2, N9). The coroner stated that this differs from hepatitis C and HIV services (N10).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The coroner directed concerns to the British Viral Hepatitis Group at the British Association for the Study of the Liver (BASL) and the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) (N9). The BASL responded on 6 July 2026, stating it does not lead guideline development and that monitoring and prescribing for chronic hepatitis B usually lies with specialist hepatology services (N11, N12). The BASL noted variation between NHS trusts regarding whether monitoring is delivered by the treating team or specialist services (N13).

analysis.brief_en: An assistant coroner in the UK has raised concerns over a lack of national guidance on prescribing and monitoring for hepatitis B reactivation following the death of a 41-year-old patient, Mr. Tung Tran. Tran, who had a renal transplant in 2013 and was diagnosed with chronic hepatitis B, died in September 2025 from complications of the virus reactivating after his entecavir prophylaxis was inadvertently discontinued. The coroner directed concerns to the British Association for the Study of the Liver and the UK Health Security Agency, noting a 'large population' of patients identified through emergency department screening but a lack of specialised commissioning to maintain engagement with services. The BASL responded that it does not lead guideline development and that monitoring and prescribing for chronic hepatitis B usually lies with specialist hepatology services, though it acknowledged variation between NHS trusts.

analysis.time: The study analyzed live births between January 2018 and December 2025 (N5). The AJMC article was published on July 14, 2026 (N32).
analysis.location_and_population: The analysis focused on 93,163 live births at three University of Pennsylvania health system hospitals in Philadelphia (N5). The affected population included newborn infants, specifically comparing male and female newborns (N1, N8, N12).
analysis.event: A retrospective cohort study investigated whether newborn sex influences parental decisions regarding vitamin K (VK) prophylaxis and hepatitis B (HBV) vaccine administration at birth (N5). The findings indicated that female newborns were more than twice as likely as boys to have their parents decline VK prophylaxis (N1, N8).
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Among the cohort, 777 infants (8.3 per 1000 births) did not receive VK prophylaxis, and 9400 (100.9 per 1000 births) did not receive the HBV birth dose (N6). VK decline rates among female newborns rose from 9.6 per 1000 births in 2018 to 19.8 per 1000 in 2025 (N11). By 2025, nearly 1 in 6 newborns did not receive the HBV birth dose (N14). The risk of life-threatening VKDB (vitamin K deficiency bleeding) increases for infants who do not receive VK prophylaxis (N2, N4).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study was conducted within a single health system, potentially limiting generalizability (N25). The authors were unable to assess subsequent clinical outcomes, such as VKDB or neonatal hepatitis B infection, beyond the birth hospitalization (N26). The authors called for additional research to better understand the observed disparities and to address sex-specific rates of newborn VK prophylaxis and HBV administration nationally (N27, N28).

analysis.brief_en: A retrospective cohort study of 93,163 live births in Philadelphia found that female newborns were more than twice as likely as boys to have their parents decline vitamin K prophylaxis, with rates rising from 9.6 to 19.8 per 1,000 births between 2018 and 2025. While the hepatitis B birth dose gap was smaller, nearly 1 in 6 newborns did not receive it by 2025. The researchers attribute the VK disparity to circumcision incentives for boys and note that a CDC policy shift allowing shared clinical decision-making for HBV may be contributing to declining uptake. The study has limitations regarding generalizability and inability to assess long-term clinical outcomes.

During a press conference on July 13, officials revealed that screening initiatives have expanded to include residents aged 40 and above who have never undergone testing, following a successful program for those aged 50 and older. Data from the 2016 Macao Health Survey indicates a 7.6 percent HBsAg positivity rate among residents aged 18 or above, with an estimated 34,000 infected individuals in the community. The bureau is collaborating with community associations to host public awareness events and will offer free anonymous rapid testing on July 25 as part of World Hepatitis Day activities. Vaccination programs since the 1980s have significantly reduced positivity rates among younger generations.

Led by WHO/Europe consultant Professor Alexander Nersesov, the course aimed to enhance the capacity of Turkmen medical professionals in combating viral hepatitis B. Participants included doctors, primary health care providers, infectious diseases specialists, and representatives from the State Medical University named after Myrat Karryev. The initiative is expected to improve patient outcomes and strengthen Turkmenistan's efforts to control and manage viral hepatitis. The training was conducted in videoconference mode and aligns with both WHO guidelines and national protocols.

analysis.location_and_population: The initiative targets residents aged 50 and above, with screening thresholds lowered to 40 years old since June 2026. It also addresses the general adult population and aims to reach over 19,000 people aged 50 and above by the end of 2025.
analysis.event: The Health Bureau (SSM) announced an expanded push to curb hepatitis B infections, including broader screening, expanded treatment access, and community outreach. This is an official public health initiative.

The initiative aims to identify silent infections earlier and reduce progression to severe liver disease, which accounts for 10.5% of cancer deaths in Macau.
